evidence: src/application/list-orders-by-state-use-case.ts: ListOrdersByStateUseCase.execute does `if (!isOrderState(state)) { throw new DomainError("validation", `Unknown order state: ${state}`); }`
src/application/get-order-use-case.ts: GetOrderUseCase.validateExecute(state: string) contains the same isOrderState check and the same DomainError("validation", `Unknown order state: ${state}`)
src/application/get-order-use-case.ts: GetOrderUseCase.execute(orderId) never calls validateExecute; the method validates order states, which has nothing to do with looking up a single order
src/application/order-dto.ts: StockLevelDto (a stock concern) is declared alongside the order DTOs and used by ListStockLevelsUseCase
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module is mostly one cohesive concern: order and stock use cases share the DTO mapping in toOrderDto and the requireOrder lookup. However, the rule that an order-state string must be valid is written out in two places. ListOrdersByStateUseCase.execute checks `isOrderState(state)` and throws `DomainError("validation", "Unknown order state: ...")`. GetOrderUseCase.validateExecute(state: string) repeats that same check and error word for word. The copy in GetOrderUseCase also doesn't fit its own class. GetOrderUseCase looks an order up by id, so validating a state string has nothing to do with it, and its own execute method never calls validateExecute. The method is an out-of-place, duplicated copy of an invariant that should live in one place, so the unit fails the rubric. A smaller issue: StockLevelDto is declared in order-dto.ts even though it describes stock levels, not orders. That blurs the file's boundary but would not fail the unit by itself.

violations.message: GetOrderUseCase.validateExecute repeats the order-state validation rule (isOrderState check + DomainError("validation", "Unknown order state")) that is already in ListOrdersByStateUseCase.execute. The method also has nothing to do with this use case's job of looking up an order by id.
The order-state validation invariant is written inline here and copied into GetOrderUseCase.validateExecute. It is not kept in a single shared place.
